pr.body:
## What does this PR do?

- generate and display backup codes during 2fa setup
- enable their use during 2fa login flow
- fix 2fa setup test to include new backup code screen

[backup-codes-setup.webm](https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/assets/55853254/3bebfb21-f7ef-4717-9135-ac30387cfb18)

[backup-codes-login.webm](https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/assets/55853254/71ef61b1-af6f-4e32-bf1e-455e52560535)

Fixes #9910
/claim #9910

## Type of change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## How should this be tested?

1. Setup 2fa to see the generated backup codes
2. Try to login with them by clicking on "Lost access"

## Mandatory Tasks

- [x] Make sure you have self-reviewed the code. A decent size PR without self-review might be rejected.

## Checklist

- I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
pr.title: feat: 2fa backup codes

raw_findings.body: The component is imported everywhere as `BackupCode` but its actual function/display name is `TwoFactor`, which is confusing during debugging and code review and could be mistaken for the real TwoFactor component
raw_findings.evidence: export default function TwoFactor({ center = true }) {
raw_findings.failure_mode: Misleading component identity reduces maintainability and increases risk of confusion when debugging
raw_findings.impact: The component is imported everywhere as `BackupCode` but its actual function/display name is `TwoFactor`, which is confusing during debugging and code review and could be mistaken for the real TwoFactor component
raw_findings.root_cause: The new file was copy-pasted from TwoFactor.tsx without renaming the function identifier
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Rename the exported function to `BackupCode` to match the file name and the import alias used throughout the codebase.
raw_findings.title: BackupCode component exported with copy-pasted function name 'TwoFactor'
raw_findings.trigger: Any developer inspecting React DevTools, error stack traces, or the component source while working on the new backup-code login/disable flow

raw_findings.body: PasswordField spreads {...props} after its internally computed `type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"}`, so the leftover `type="password"` prop (kept from the previous TextField usage) always overrides the toggle, meaning the password is never revealed even after clicking the eye icon
raw_findings.failure_mode: Show/hide password feature silently does nothing despite the eye icon being rendered
raw_findings.impact: PasswordField spreads {...props} after its internally computed `type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"}`, so the leftover `type="password"` prop (kept from the previous TextField usage) always overrides the toggle, meaning the password is never revealed even after clicking the eye icon
raw_findings.root_cause: TextField was swapped for PasswordField but the explicit type="password" prop required by TextField was left in place, and PasswordField's prop-spread order lets caller props override its internal visibility state
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the now-unnecessary `type="password"` prop from this PasswordField usage; PasswordField manages the input type internally.
raw_findings.title: Redundant type="password" prop breaks PasswordField's show/hide toggle
raw_findings.trigger: User opens the Enable 2FA modal and clicks the eye icon on the password field to reveal the typed password

raw_findings.body: The created object URL is only revoked the next time handleSetup runs; if the modal is simply closed or the component unmounts, the Blob URL is never released, leaking browser memory tied to that Blob
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unreleased Blob URLs accumulate over repeated open/setup/close cycles
raw_findings.impact: The created object URL is only revoked the next time handleSetup runs; if the modal is simply closed or the component unmounts, the Blob URL is never released, leaking browser memory tied to that Blob
raw_findings.root_cause: Revocation logic is coupled only to a subsequent call of handleSetup rather than to modal close or component unmount
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Revoke backupCodesUrl in resetState() and/or in a useEffect cleanup on unmount so the object URL is always released when the modal closes.
raw_findings.title: Backup codes Blob object URL is never revoked on modal close/unmount
raw_findings.trigger: User completes 2FA setup once (creating a Blob URL for the backup-codes download link) and then closes/cancels the modal or navigates away without triggering setup again

raw_findings.body: Regressions in the new backup-code authentication or disable logic would not be caught by the e2e suite
raw_findings.evidence: // TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup
raw_findings.failure_mode: Critical new authentication code path ships without automated verification
raw_findings.impact: Regressions in the new backup-code authentication or disable logic would not be caught by the e2e suite
raw_findings.root_cause: New authentication path added without corresponding e2e test coverage, as acknowledged by the author's own TODO
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add e2e test steps that capture a generated backup code, log out, log back in via 'Lost access' + the backup code, and separately disable 2FA using a backup code.
raw_findings.title: No e2e coverage for logging in or disabling 2FA using a backup code
raw_findings.trigger: The PR introduces backup-code based login (credentials.backupCode in next-auth-options.ts) and backup-code based 2FA disable (backupCode in disable.ts), but the only added test steps exercise the setup UI (download/copy/close), never an actual login or disable using a generated backup code

raw_findings.body: A bug that corrupts, mis-formats, or omits backup codes in the downloaded file would go undetected
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent data-correctness regression in the downloaded backup codes file
raw_findings.impact: A bug that corrupts, mis-formats, or omits backup codes in the downloaded file would go undetected
raw_findings.root_cause: Test only checks download.suggestedFilename() rather than the file body, per the added TODO
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Read the downloaded file in the test and assert its content matches the expected formatted backup codes.
raw_findings.title: Downloaded backup-codes file content is not verified in test
raw_findings.trigger: Test clicks the backup-codes-download button and only asserts the suggested filename, never reading the file's actual contents

raw_findings.body: A bug that copies wrong, malformed, or partial backup codes to the clipboard would go undetected
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent data-correctness regression in the copy-to-clipboard feature
raw_findings.impact: A bug that copies wrong, malformed, or partial backup codes to the clipboard would go undetected
raw_findings.root_cause: Test only checks for the success toast rather than the actual clipboard payload, per the added TODO
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Read the clipboard content in the test (e.g., via page.evaluate(() => navigator.clipboard.readText())) and assert it matches the expected formatted backup codes.
raw_findings.title: Copied clipboard content of backup codes is not verified in test
raw_findings.trigger: Test clicks the backup-codes-copy button and only asserts the success toast appears, never verifying what was actually written to the clipboard

raw_findings.impact: DisplayBackupCodes is declared second even though it is actually the last step shown to the user, which can mislead future maintainers reasoning about or refactoring the step flow

validated_findings.suggested_fix: Move the DisplayBackupCodes member to the end of the enum, after EnterTotpCode, so declaration order matches the actual UI sequence.
validated_findings.title: New DisplayBackupCodes enum value placed out of the actual step flow order
validated_findings.trigger: A developer reads the SetupStep enum expecting its declaration order to reflect the UI flow (ConfirmPassword -> DisplayQrCode -> EnterTotpCode -> DisplayBackupCodes)
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The enum order claim is subjective. Looking at the actual flow: ConfirmPassword -> DisplayQrCode -> EnterTotpCode -> DisplayBackupCodes. The enum declares DisplayBackupCodes at position 1 (after ConfirmPassword). However, enum numeric values don't affect runtime behavior, and the actual step transitions are controlled by setStep calls, not enum order. This is a minor stylistic preference with no functional impact.
